'''''UFC 331: Van vs. Pantoja 2''''' (branded as '''''Crypto.com UFC 331''''' for sponsorship reasons) was a [[mixed martial arts]] event produced by the [[Ultimate Fighting Championship]] that took place on September 19, 2026, at [[Crypto.com Arena]] in [[Los Angeles]], California, United States.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Crypto.com Arena in LA gastheer voor UFC 331 op 19 september|url=https://www.vechtsportinfo.nl/nieuws/ufc-331-crypto-arena-los-angeles|date=2026-07-13|access-date=2026-07-14|publisher=vechtsportinfo.nl|author=Ruben Kok}} {{in lang|nl}}</ref>

==Background==
The event marked the promotion's sixth visit to Los Angeles and first since [[UFC 227]] in August 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/ufc/article/ufc-returns-to-los-angeles-for-ufc-331-in-september/|title=UFC returns to Los Angeles for UFC 331 in September|publisher=sportsnet.ca|author=Staff|date=2026-08-01|access-date=2026-08-02}}</ref> Initial reports had speculated that the event may have been held at [[Intuit Dome]] in [[Inglewood, California]], or be part of the promotion's [[Noche UFC]] 4 celebration of [[Mexican Independence Day]] in [[Glendale, Arizona]].<ref name="UFC331">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/ufc/article/canadas-charles-jourdain-to-face-marlon-vera-at-ufc-331-in-september/|title=Canada's Charles Jourdain to face Marlon Vera at UFC 331 in September|publisher=sportsnet.ca|author=Staff|date=2026-07-07|access-date=2026-07-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mmamania.com/ufc-fight-announcements/455357/marlon-vera-vs-charles-jourdain-booked-for-ufc-331-on-sept-19|title=Marlon Vera vs. Charles Jourdain booked for Noche UFC 4 date|publisher=mmamania.com|author=Alexander Behunin|date=2026-07-07|access-date=2026-07-08}}</ref>

A [[UFC Flyweight Championship]] rematch between current champion [[Joshua Van]] and former champion [[Alexandre Pantoja]] headlined the event.<ref>{{Cite web|title=UFC 331 gets Joshua Van vs. Alexandre Pantoja rematch|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/story/sports/ufc/2026/08/05/ufc-331-gets-joshua-van-vs-alexandre-pantoja-rematch/91173360007/|date=2026-08-05|access-date=2026-08-05|publisher=mmajunkie.usatoday.com|author=Nolan King}}</ref> They previously competed in December 2025 at [[UFC 323]], where Van won the belt via technical knockout 26 seconds into the first round as a result of an arm injury sustained by Pantoja.<ref>{{Cite web|title=UFC 323: Alexandre Pantoja injures arm, Joshua Van claims gold|url=https://cagesidepress.com/2025/12/07/ufc-323-alexandre-pantoja-injures-arm-joshua-van-claims-gold/|date=2025-12-07|access-date=2026-07-15|publisher=cagesidepress.com|author=Jay Anderson}}</ref>

A five-round lightweight bout between [[Arman Tsarukyan]] and [[Maurício Ruffy]] served as the co-main event.<ref name="Tsarukyan-Ruffy">{{Cite web|title=Arman Tsarukyan vs. Mauricio Ruffy five-round bout among UFC 331 additions|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/story/sports/ufc/2026/08/05/ufc-331-arman-tsarukyan-vs-mauricio-ruffy-five-round-bout-set/91190598007/|date=2026-08-05|access-date=2026-08-05|publisher=mmajunkie.usatoday.com|author=Mike Bohn}}</ref> Tsarukyan was initially expected to face former [[UFC Lightweight Championship|UFC Lightweight Champion]] [[Charles Oliveira]] also in a five-round lightweight bout, with early reports indicating that Oliveira would defend his symbolic "[[List of UFC champions#BMF Title|BMF]]" (''baddest [[motherfucker]]'') title, but the bout was later changed to a non-title contest.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.telecomasia.net/news/mma/oliveira-tsarukyan-rematch-ufc-331-september-19/|title=Oliveira and Tsarukyan set for BMF title rematch at UFC 331 on September 19|publisher=telecomasia.net|author=Anastasiia Dudkina|date=2026-07-25|access-date=2026-07-29}}</ref><ref name="OliveiraTsarukyan">{{Cite web|url=https://bloodyelbow.com/2026/08/01/arman-tsarukyan-reportedly-wont-be-allowed-to-challenge-for-charles-oliveiras-bmf-title-at-ufc-331/|title=Arman Tsarukyan reportedly won't be allowed to challenge for Charles Oliveira's BMF title at UFC 331|publisher=bloodyelbow.com|author=Harvey Leonard|date=2026-08-01|access-date=2026-08-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Arman Tsarukyan title fight reportedly set to headline UFC 331 in Los Angeles|url=https://bloodyelbow.com/2026/07/23/arman-tsarukyan-title-fight-reportedly-set-to-headline-ufc-331-in-los-angeles/|date=2026-07-23|access-date=2026-07-24|publisher=bloodyelbow.com|author=Kyle Dimond}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Report: Arman Tsarukyan vs. Charles Oliveira 2 tops UFC 331 in LA|url=https://www.mmamania.com/ufc-fight-announcements/460592/report-arman-tsarukyan-vs-charles-oliveira-2-tops-ufc-331-in-la|date=2026-07-28|access-date=2026-07-28|publisher=mmamania.com|author=Alexander Behunin}}</ref> Oliveira and Tsarukyan previously met in April 2024 at [[UFC 300]], where Tsarukyan won via split decision.<ref>{{Cite web|title=UFC 300: Arman Tsarukyan takes next step, defeats ex-champ Charles Oliveira|url=https://cagesidepress.com/2024/04/13/ufc-300-arman-tsarukyan-takes-next-step-defeats-ex-champ-charles-oliveira/|date=2024-04-13|access-date=2026-07-24|publisher=cagesidepress.com|author=Patrick McCorry}}</ref> On August 5, the promotion announced that Tsarukyan would instead face Ruffy. The withdrawal came just days after the death of Oliveira's longtime teammate, UFC flyweight [[Allan Nascimento]], although no official reason for Oliveira's withdrawal was given.<ref name="Tsarukyan-Ruffy"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/story/sports/ufc/2026/08/03/ufc-fighter-allan-nascimento-dead-heart-attack/91157894007/|title=UFC announces flyweight Allan Nascimento dead at 34|publisher=mmajunkie.usatoday.com|author=Nolan King|date=2026-08-03|access-date=2026-08-06}}</ref>

A [[UFC Women's Bantamweight Championship]] bout between the reigning champion [[Kayla Harrison]] (who is also a [[Judo at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's 78 kg|2012]] and [[Judo at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 78 kg|2016 Olympic gold medalist in judo]]; and a two-time [[Professional Fighters League|PFL]] women's lightweight tournament champion) and former two-time champion [[Amanda Nunes]], who also held the [[UFC Women's Featherweight Championship]], was reportedly planned for the event.<ref name="OliveiraTsarukyan"/> However, the bout is postponed for undisclosed reasons.<ref name="OliveiraTsarukyan"/> The bout was originally scheduled for [[UFC 324]] in January 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/story/sports/ufc/2025/11/27/ufc-324-kayla-harrison-vs-amanda-nunes-booked-paramount-debut/87487847007/|title=Kayla Harrison vs. Amanda Nunes title bout set for UFC 324 co-main|publisher=mmajunkie.usatoday.com|author=Matthew Wells and Nolan King|date=2025-11-27|access-date=2026-08-01}}</ref> However, Harrison withdrew from the bout after being diagnosed with herniated discs in her neck, which required surgery.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/ufc/466164/report-kayla-harrison-out-of-ufc-324-fight-against-amanda-nunes-postponed-to-later-date|title=Kayla Harrison out of UFC 324, fight against Amanda Nunes postponed to later date|publisher=mmafighting.com|author=Damon Martin|date=2026-01-14|access-date=2026-08-01}}</ref>

A bantamweight bout between former [[UFC Bantamweight Championship]] challenger [[Marlon Vera]] and [[Charles Jourdain]] took place at the event.<ref name="UFC331"/> The bout was originally scheduled to take place at [[UFC Fight Night: du Plessis vs. Usman]] in July, but was moved to this event for undisclosed reasons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/mma/news/ufc-oklahoma-city-reportedly-gets-banger-co-main-fight-after-main-event-announcement|title=UFC Oklahoma City reportedly gets banger co-main fight after main event announcement|publisher=si.com|author=Drew Beaupre|date=2026-06-23|access-date=2026-07-09}}</ref>

A heavyweight bout between former interim [[UFC Heavyweight Championship]] challenger [[Curtis Blaydes]] and former [[Legacy Fighting Alliance#LFA Heavyweight Championship|LFA Heavyweight Champion]] [[Waldo Cortes-Acosta]] was scheduled for the event.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260713031204/https://heavy.com/sports/ufc/top-8-ufc-331-los-angeles/|title=Top 8 heavyweights collide at UFC 331 in Los Angeles|publisher=heavy.com|author=Marcel Dorff|date=2026-07-12|access-date=2026-07-14}}</ref> However, the bout actually took place one week prior at [[UFC Fight Night: Silva vs. Delgado]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://heavy.com/sports/ufc/top-8-heavyweights-collide-at-noche-ufc-in-phoenix/|title=Top 8 Heavyweights collide at Noche UFC in Phoenix|publisher=heavy.com|author=Marcel Dorff|date=2026-07-14|access-date=2026-07-14}}</ref>

A lightweight rematch between former lightweight title challenger [[Renato Moicano]] and former [[UFC Featherweight Championship]] challenger [[Brian Ortega]] was scheduled for the main card.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/ufc/501057/renato-moicano-vs-brian-ortega-rematch-targeted-for-ufc-331|title=Renato Moicano vs. Brian Ortega rematch targeted for UFC 331|publisher=mmafighting.com|author=Jed Meshew|date=2026-07-24|access-date=2026-07-24}}</ref> However, days before the event, Ortega had to withdraw due to an eye injury, so Moicano was re-scheduled to headline [[UFC Fight Night: Moicano vs. Nolan]] against [[Tom Nolan (fighter)|Tom Nolan]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/story/sports/ufc/2026/09/14/ufc-331-renato-moicano-vs-brian-ortega-tom-nolan/91768221007/|title=UFC 331 loses main card bout days before event; one fighter gets future main event|publisher=mmajunkie.usatoday.com|author=Nolan King|date=2026-09-14|access-date=2026-09-15}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/story/sports/ufc/2026/09/16/brian-ortega-reveals-freak-accident-which-led-to-ufc-331-withdrawal/91787845007/|title=Brian Ortega: Headbutt during jiu-jitsu caused cut, UFC 331 withdrawal|publisher=mmajunkie.usatoday.com|author=Farah Hannoun|date=2026-09-16|access-date=2026-09-17}}</ref> The pair previously met in a featherweight bout at [[UFC 214]] in July 2017, where Ortega won via third‑round guillotine choke.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2017/07/ufc-214-results-brian-ortega-record-fourth-straight-win-by-third-round-finish|title=UFC 214 results: Brian Ortega earns record 4th straight win by 3rd-round finish vs. Renato Moicano|publisher=mmajunkie.usatoday.com|author=Ben Fowlkes|date=2017-07-29|access-date=2026-07-24}}</ref> They were previously expected to rematch at [[UFC 326]] in March,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mmamania.com/ufc-news/409489/report-brian-ortega-finally-makes-move-to-lightweight-draws-renato-moicano-at-ufc-326-on-march-7|title=Report: Brian Ortega finally makes move to lightweight, draws Renato Moicano at UFC 326 on March 7|publisher=mmamania.com|author=Dan Hiergesell|date=2025-12-13|access-date=2026-07-24}}</ref> but Ortega withdrew due to injury and Moicano was later moved to headline [[UFC Fight Night: Moicano vs. Duncan]] one month afterward.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/story/sports/ufc/2026/01/30/ufc-326-news-fight-card-brian-ortega-out-vs-renato-moicano/88399814007/|title=Brian Ortega withdraws from UFC 326|publisher=mmajunkie.usatoday.com|author=Nolan King|date=2026-01-30|access-date=2026-07-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/story/sports/ufc/2026/02/21/ufc-books-renato-moicano-vs-chris-duncan-april-main-event/88800800007/|title=UFC books American Top Team stablemates for April main event|publisher=mmajunkie.usatoday.com|author=Nolan King|date=2026-02-21|access-date=2026-07-24}}</ref>

==Bonus awards==
In addition to the standard $100,000 Fight of the Night and Performance of the Night bonuses, UFC CEO [[Dana White]] announced a one-time "Proper Chaos Bonus" of $50,000, tied to the season two premiere of the [[Paramount+]] series [[MobLand]], which aired the night before the event. The winner was determined at White's discretion.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/story/sports/ufc/2026/09/14/dana-white-announces-new-50000-bonus-for-ufc-331-in-honor-of-mobland/91766906007/|title=Dana White announces special $50,000 'proper chaos bonus' for UFC 331|publisher=mmajunkie.usatoday.com|author=Danny Segura|date=2026-09-14|access-date=2026-09-16}}</ref>

The following fighters received $100,000 bonuses (during the post-fight press conference, White matched the "Proper Chaos Bonus" to $100,000). The other finishes received $25,000 additional bonuses.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mmamania.com/ufc-331-fight-card-start-time-date-location-van-vs-pantoja-2/473405/official-post-fight-bonus-winners-ufc-331-results-paramount-proper-chaos-van-pantoja-sharaf-o-neill-tsarukyan|title=Bonuses! Sean Sharaf banks $100K for improbable knockout win over Gable Steveson|publisher=mmamania.com|author=Dan Hiergesell|date=2026-09-20|access-date=2026-09-20}}</ref>
* '''Fight of the Night:''' '''Joshua Van vs. Alexandre Pantoja'''
* '''Performance of the Night:''' '''Arman Tsarukyan''' and '''Casey O'Neill'''
* '''"Proper Chaos Bonus": Sean Sharaf'''

==Reported payout==
The following is the reported payout to the fighters as reported by the [[California State Athletic Commission]]. The amounts do not include sponsor money, discretionary bonuses, viewership points, or additional earnings.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/ufc/511404/ufc-331-salaries-revealed-alexandre-pantoja-joshua-van-lead-all-fighters|title=UFC 331 salaries revealed: Alexandre Pantoja, Joshua Van lead all fighters|publisher=mmafighting.com|author=Damon Martin|date=2026-09-20|access-date=2026-09-20}}</ref>

*'''Joshua Van''': $500,000 (no win bonus) def. Alexandre Pantoja: $650,000
*'''Arman Tsarukyan''': $350,000 (no win bonus) def. Maurício Ruffy: $110,000
*'''Patrício Pitbull''': $400,000 (includes $200,000 win bonus) def. Choi Doo-ho: $85,000
*'''Sean Sharaf''': $60,000 (includes $30,000 win bonus) def. Gable Steveson: $160,000
*'''Alonzo Menifield''': $310,000 (includes $155,000 win bonus) def. Iwo Baraniewski: $50,000
*'''Marlon Vera''': $400,000 (includes $200,000 win bonus) def. Charles Jourdain: $108,000
*'''Robelis Despaigne''': $200,000 (includes $100,000 win bonus) def. Tai Tuivasa: $350,000
*'''Michael Aswell Jr.''': $60,000 (includes $30,000 win bonus) def. Yoo Joo-sang: $12,000
*'''Ryan Gandra''': $28,000 (includes $14,000 win bonus) def. Osman Diaz: $25,000
*'''Edmen Shahbazyan''': $250,000 (includes $125,000 win bonus) def. Brunno Ferreira: $95,000
*'''Casey O'Neill''': $132,000 (includes $66,000 win bonus) def. Eduarda Moura: $33,000
*'''Joanderson Brito''': $158,000 (includes $79,000 win bonus) def. Giga Chikadze: $93,000
